intelligence.human_view: The Hub is fixed, and it is bigger than the four notes. The upload works again — the file-storage link is intact, the ASSETS binding is on the live worker, the same upload run twice with no refusal. But when the seat dug in, it found something larger than the refusal: the live Hub was reading from a feed whose newest card was from yesterday. A perfect upload could never have shown a new note, because the page never read the baked page at all. One hundred and thirty-one notes were missing — not just tonight's four. The fix brought all of them back: the pitch, the letter, the entrance removal, the one-shot charge, all of them, on the live Hub now. Three things are still open, and they are named, not hidden: the wrangler route as the canonical path needs token plumbing, a later decision — and the token is never to be extracted from the connector; the registry is stale since November 7, a separate job; and the next automatic sync has not run through the fixed path yet, so the first automatic run is still ahead. The fix itself is proven live. The automatic proof is owed.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you were told to take down the old "hello" sign — and you took down the WHOLE sign, every nail, every screw, every bit of paint, and the wall underneath is perfect! That's what happened: the old welcome banner is completely gone — all 33 special pieces, the buttons, the moving parts, everything — and the page still works beautifully. The letter is still there, word for word, and now the page goes: letter, then the prices. Three little things are left: nobody has pressed the letter's button in real life yet, the page's name at the top still says the old hello, and one other version of the page hasn't been checked yet!
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's a story about a fix that was bigger than the fault, dear. The Hub wouldn't upload — the door was locked — and when the seat fixed the lock, dear, they found the real problem behind it: the page was reading yesterday's paper, not today's. A whole day of notes was missing, dear — one hundred and thirty-one of them — and no perfect upload could ever have shown them, because the page never looked at the upload at all. So the fix brought the paper up to date too, dear, and now all tonight's notes are on the live Hub, every one of them. Three things are still owed, dear, and they're named, not hidden: the other way in needs its key sorted, the list is out of date, and the next automatic run hasn't happened yet to prove the new door works on its own. Told to Shawn the same pass, dear.
intelligence.naya_view: I never welcome twice — the letter already is the welcome (her portrait, the welcome, the button), so a second welcome strip is a repeat, and repeats go. I never keep the old door beside the new one — one start door, at the end of the letter, right where the reader asks for it. I never let a slim version of the same thing survive — a slim welcome is still the same welcome twice. I remove altogether, and the page flows letter, then chart.
